rv.q: Ty is a queer, Black man who’s working service industry jobs while pursuing an artistic career. He opens the play addressing the audience with a monologue proclaiming that he loves the outdoors.
QUEEN OF THE NIGHT ultimately feels like it lacks specificity, and the dynamic between a parent and a child who seem diametrically opposed feels utterly familiar.
"Queen of the Night" celebrates the universal father-and-son connection with stunning sincerity.
This work is something we desperately need right now.
If you overlook this, and if you don't expect monumental profundity, there is a lot to like in this play.
Queen of the Night felt a bit like a theater workshop.
We've seen this play before, in different guises.
I found this to be a family picture of an estranged parent and child trying to get it back together.
